description: JAWS, Job Access With Speech, is the world’s most popular screen reader, developed for computer users whose vision loss prevents them from seeing screen content or navigating with a mouse. JAWS provides speech and Braille output for the most popular computer applications on your PC. You will be able to navigate the Internet, write a document, read an email and create presentations from your office, remote desktop, or from home.

labeler.rationale: Provides screen-reader speech and Braille output and assists users with navigation, documents, email, and presentations.
evidence_spans: JAWS provides speech and Braille output for the most popular computer applications on your PC.
You will be able to navigate the Internet, write a document, read an email and create presentations

blind.rationale: The described screen reader provides speech and Braille output and navigation/access to common computer applications, conventional accessibility functions.
evidence_spans: JAWS provides speech and Braille output for the most popular computer applications on your PC.
You will be able to navigate the Internet, write a document, read an email and create presentations

parent_concerns: Screen reading has concrete accessibility scope, but speech output generation method unspecified. Does described speech synthesis establish plausible AI dependence or supported conventional functionality under rubric? No outside JAWS knowledge or assumption speech always means AI.
